\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Fourier Concentration}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.FourierConcentration
\section{Overview}

This module proves O'Donnell's Lemma 4.21: if a Boolean function $f$ on $n$ variables
becomes a shallow decision tree with high probability under a Bernoulli($p$)-random
restriction, then the Fourier spectrum of its $\pm1$-encoding is concentrated on low
degrees. Concretely, if $\varepsilon$ is the probability that the restricted function
requires decision-tree depth at least $k$, then the Fourier weight of $\sigma\circ f$
above degree $3k/p$ is at most $4\varepsilon$; the supporting lemmas partition tail
events over intersection patterns and aggregate the expected restricted spectrum.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

\difficulty{2}
For every function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, the real-valued function obtained by mapping
false to $1$ and true to $-1$ after applying $g$ takes values only in $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Nonnegativity of restriction-event probabilities]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.bernoulliRestrProb_nonneg}
\label{RestrictionFourier.bernoulliRestrProb_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma.Restriction, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg'}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0\le p\le 1$, and let $E$ be
a decidable event on restrictions of the $n$ variables. The Bernoulli restriction
probability of $E$, formed using the weights $p^{|J|}((1-p)/2)^{n-|J|}$ for a
restriction with free-variable set $J$, is nonnegative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Partitioning by intersection size]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.sum_prob_inter_eq_card_ge}
\label{RestrictionFourier.sum_prob_inter_eq_card_ge}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma.Restriction, SwitchingLemma.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in\mathbb{R}$, let $U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and
let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Summing, over all subsets $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ with
$|S|\ge k$, the Bernoulli restriction probability that $U\cap J=S$ gives the Bernoulli
restriction probability that $|U\cap J|\ge k$, where $J$ is the free-variable set of the
restriction. This identity holds for every real $p$.
\end{lemma}

  {RestrictionFourier.sum_prob_inter_eq_card_ge}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b005}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p\in\mathbb{R}$, let $F:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and
let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. The sum over all frequencies $S$ with $|S|\ge k$ of the
Bernoulli-weighted squared Fourier coefficients of the restrictions $F_\rho$ equals
$\sum_{U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\widehat F(U)^2$ times the Bernoulli restriction
probability that $|U\cap J|\ge k$, where $J$ denotes the free-variable set of the
restriction. Explicitly, this identity is
\[\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\},\ |S|\ge k}\ \sum_\rho w_p(\rho)\widehat{F_\rho}(S)^2=\sum_{U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\widehat F(U)^2\Pr_\rho[|U\cap J|\ge k],\]
with $w_p(\rho)=p^{|J|}((1-p)/2)^{n-|J|}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier concentration from random restrictions]
\lean{RestrictionFourier.odonnell_lemma_4_21}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b003
}
\label{RestrictionFourier.odonnell_lemma_4_21}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one, DecisionTree.degree_le_dtDepth, RestrictionFourier.bernoulliRestrProb_card_inter_ge, RestrictionFourier.bernoulliRestrProb_nonneg, RestrictionFourier.isPmOne_boolToSign, RestrictionFourier.restrictBF, RestrictionFourier.restrictBF_boolToSign, RestrictionFourier.sum_tail_expectation_eq, SwitchingLemma.Restriction, SwitchingLemma.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrWeight, SwitchingLemma.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg', SwitchingLemma.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{5}
This is O'Donnell's Lemma 4.21, with constant $4$ in place of $3$. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n
\to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $p \in \bbr$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $k
\in \bbn$ with $k \ge 1$. Let $\rho$ be a Bernoulli($p$)-random restriction on $n$
variables: each coordinate is independently left free with probability $p$ and
otherwise fixed to a uniformly random bit, so a restriction with free-variable set $J$
has probability $p^{\abs{J}}\bigl(\tfrac{1-p}{2}\bigr)^{\,n-\abs{J}}$. Write $f_\rho$
for the function obtained from $f$ by fixing the coordinates outside $J$ according to
$\rho$, $\mathrm{DT}(g)$ for the least depth of a decision tree computing a Boolean
function $g$, and $\sigma$ for the sign encoding ($\sigma(\mathtt{false}) = 1$,
$\sigma(\mathtt{true}) = -1$). Setting
$\varepsilon = \Pr_\rho\bigl[\mathrm{DT}(f_\rho) \ge k\bigr]$, the Fourier spectrum of
the $\pm1$-encoding $\sigma \circ f$ is $4\varepsilon$-concentrated below degree
$3k/p$:
\[
  \sum_{\substack{U \subseteq [n] \\ 3k \le p\,\abs{U}}}
    \widehat{\sigma \circ f}(U)^2 \;\le\; 4\,\varepsilon,
\]
where the degree condition is stated division-free as $3k \le p\,\abs{U}$.
\end{theorem}
